house, in came a man who greeted us. The Messenger of God (SAAS) got up in
a fright, and I arose too; suddenly, there was Dihya al-Kalbi. He (the Messenger
of God (SAAS)), said, 'This is Gabriel! He has ordered me to attack Banii
Qurayza. He said to me, "You have put down your arms, but we have not.'" We
had pursued the polytheists until we reached Hamra' al-Asad, following the
return of the Messenger of God (SAAS) from al-khandaq. So the Messenger of
God (SAAS) arose in great concern and said to his Companions, 'I require you
not to perform the al-'asr prayer until you arrive at Banii Qurayza.' The sun
set before they reached them and one group of the Muslims thought that the
Messenger of God (SAAS) had not wanted them to wait to say the prayer and
so they prayed. Another group maintained that they were acting in accord with
the requirement made by the Messenger of God (SAAS), and that they would
not be considered guilty of a sin for not praying. And so one group did pray, in
their faith and as a precaution, while another group did not, for the same reasons.
The Messenger of God (SAAS) did not berate any person from either group.
He then went forth and as he passed by any group of people, on his way to Banii
Qurayza, he would ask them, 'Did anyone pass by you?' They responded, 'Dihya
al-Kalbi passed by on his grey mule, mounted on a piece of brocade cloth.' He
responded, 'That was Gabriel; he has been sent to Bann Qurayza to shake them
up, and to cast terror into them.'
"The Messenger of God (SAAS) then besieged them, telling his Companions
to protect him with their shields so that he could hear their response. He called
out to them, 'Hey, you, you brothers of monkeys and pigs!' They replied, 'Abn
al-Qsim, you used not to employ bad language!'
"And so he besieged them until they came down, following the judgement of
Sa'd b. Mu'adh, whose allies they were. He decreed for them that their warriors
should be killed and that their children and women should become captive."
This _**hadith**_ has excellent lines of transmission from 'A'isha and others.


The scholars differ over which of the two groups was correct that day. In fact
the consensus is that each of them was worthy and justified in their actions and
not to be severely criticized.
One group of scholars, however, maintains that those who postponed the
prayer from its predetermined time until they could perform it among Banii
Qurayza were correct, because their order to postpone it that day was specific
and special and therefore should have been given precedence over the normal
time for which it was determined under the law.

Abn Muhammad b. **Hann** al-Z&iri stated in his biography (of the Prophet
(SAAS)), "God knows that had we been there we would not have performed the


**IMAM ABU AL-FIDA' ISMA'IL IBN** **KATHiR** **161**


_al-'asr_ prayer unless it had been among Banii Qurayza, even if it would have
had to be several days thereafter!"
This statement of his accords with the principle he holds fundamental, to act
in accord with what is apparent.
Another group of scholars considered, on the contrary, that those who
performed the prayer at its regular time while they were travelling were the ones
who were correct because they had understood that the intent was to hasten their
journey to Banii Qurayza and not to postpone the prayer. They acted in accord
with the precepts suggesting the superiority of prayer being performed at its
proper time, even though they understood what the legislator had wanted.
Because of this, he did not berate them or order them to repeat the prayer at the
time to which it had been changed that day, as the others claimed. Those who did
postpone it were forgiven, since they acted in accord with their understanding;
most things they were ordered to do they did in fact accomplish.
As for those who maintain that it is permissible to postpone prayer because of
warfare - as al-Bukhi~ri understood and justified from the _**hadith**_ of Ibn Wmar
referred to previously - (in this case) neither those who performed the prayer
earlier nor those who did so later ought to be considered suspect. But God knows
best.


Ibn Ishiiq then stated, "The Messenger of God (SAAS) thereafter sent forward

Masii h. Wqha stated in his work on the _maghdzi,_ the military expeditions,

Ibn Ishaq stated, "The Messenger of God (SAAS) made camp at one of the

satisfaction over Banii Qurayza!' These people had been his allies and colleagues
before Islam. Then his wound stopped bleeding and God sent the gale against
the polytheists and spared the believers engaging in battle; God is indeed
powerful, strong. Abii Sufym and his force then went to Tihma, while Wyayna
b. Badr and his force withdrew to Najd.
"Banii Qurayza then returned home and sought protection in their fortresses.
The Messenger of God (SAAS) returned to Medina where he ordered a leather
tent he set up in the mosque for Sa'd. Then Gabriel came, the folds of his
clothing covered with dust, and he said, 'Have yon put down your weapons,
then? By God, the angels haven't put down their weapons yet. Go forth and do
battle with Banii Quray~a!'

"The Messenger of God (SAAS) then put on his breast-plate and had it
announced that the men should prepare to depart for battle. He passed by Bana

al-Kalhi was similar in beard, age and face to Gabriel, upon whom be peace.
"The Messenger of God (SAAS) proceeded on to Banii Qurayza and besieged
them for 25 days. When their suffering from the siege grew intense, a message

was sent telling them to accept the authority of the Messenger of God (SAAS).

'A'isha went on, "His wound then burst; up to then he had been free of it,

'... compassionate among themselves'"(sizrat al-Fath; XLVIII, v.29).

'Alqama stated, "I then asked, 'How did the Messenger of God (SAAS)
ream?' 'A'isha replied, LHis eyes never wept for anyone. However, if he was deeply

The chain of authorities for this hadith is excellent, and there are testimonials
to its veracity from other sources. In it there is the clear statement that Sa'd
prayed twice, once before he passed judgement on Bann Qurayza, and once
thereafter, as we stated earlier. And all praise and credit go to God. We will
report, after finishing the narrative, the manner of his death and burial, and the
credit to him therefore, may God be pleased with him and give him pleasure.

It has been related above that Hihbm b. al-'Ariqa, God damn him, had shot an

enemy clans. When the latter withdrew, dispersing away from Medina, Bann
Qurayza were totally left to disaster, both on earth and in the after-life. The
Messenger of God (SAAS) went to them and besieged them, as told above.
When they were in real suffering, beset from all sides, they decided to submit to
the authority of the Messenger of God (SAAS) to do with them as ever God
wished. He delegated that authority to the chief of Aws, who had been allied
with them before the coming of Islam; he was Sacd h. Musdh. Banii Quray~a
were pleased with this. It is said that they initially gave themselves over to Sacd's
authority because they had high hopes of his kindness and partiality towards
them. They did not know that they were more hateful in his view than the apes
and pigs that were their peers! This was because of the intensity of his faith, and
his high trust. May God be pleased with him and give him pleasure.
The Messenger of God (SAAS) sent for him; Sa'd was in a tent in the
mosque. He was brought on a donkey riding on a soft saddle placed under h i
because of his injury. When he drew near the tent of the Messenger of God
(SAAS), the latter ordered all there to rise for _**`hi.`**_ It was said that this was
so that he would dismount because of the severity of his injury; also it was said

(SAAS) was asked about this, and he said, "No; but the angels carried him."'"
(This has) an excellent line of transmission.
Al-Bukhari stated, "Muhammad b. Bashshar related to us, quoting Ghundar,
quoting Shu'ba, from Abii Ishzq (who said), 'I heard al-Bar9 bb.Azib say, "I was
presented with a silk robe for the Prophet (SAAS), and his Companions began
touching it and admiring its softness. He said, 'Are you admiring the softness
of this? The kerchiefs of Sa'd b. Musdh are better than them, or softer.'"'"
He (the source) then said, "Qatzda related this, as did al-Zuhri who reported
hearing it from Anas, from the Prophet (SAAS)."

Alpnad stated, "'Ahd al-Wahhzb related to us, from Sa'id, he being the son
of Abn 'Uriiba, from Qatzda, from Anas b. Mdik, that Ukaydir Duma made a
present of a jubba, a long outer garment, to the Messenger of God (SAAS); this
was before the wearing of silk was prohibited. He put it on and when people
admired it, he said, 'By Him in whose hands is my soul, the kerchiefs of Sa'd in
heaven are finer than this!"'

This hadith accords with the criteria of both al-Bukhzri and Muslim, hut they
did not include it. Al-Bukhzri, however, quoted it as commentary.

Ahmad stated that Yazid quoted Muhammad b. 'Amr as follows, "Waqid b.
'Amr h. Sa'd b. Mu47dh related to me (and Muhammmad said that Wzqid was
one of the finest, best and tallest of men) as follows, 'I went in to Anas b. Mdik
and he asked me who I was. I replied that I was Wzqid, son of 'Amr, the son of
Sacd b. Muzdh. He then said, "You take after Sa'd." He then wept copiously,
saying, "May God grant Sa'd His mercy! He was one of the finest and tallest of
men." He then went on, "The Messenger of God (SAAS) dispatched an army
out to fight Ukaydir Diima, who sent to him ajubba of brocade woven with gold
thread. The Messenger of God (SAAS) put it on, went up on to the mmbar, the
pulpit, and sat down without speaking. He then came down again. People felt
and gazed admiringly at thejubba, and the Messenger of God (SAAS) asked
them, 'So you admire this then? The kerchiefs of Sa'd h. Mu47dh in heaven are
much finer than what you can now see."""
Al-Tirmidhi related it thus, as did al-Nasa'i, from a hadith of Muhammad b.
'Amr. Al-Tirmidhi classified it as hasan ~ahih, "good and authentic".

I would comment that Sa'd's death came some _**25**_ days after the withdrawal
of the _ahzab,_ the enemy clans. They had assembled in Shawwd of _**5**_ AH, as
is told above, and remained there for approximately 1 month. Thereafter, the
Messenger of God (SAAS) went forth and besieged Banii Qurayza for some
_**25**_ days. They then accepted the authority of Sa'd, who died shortly after he
had passed judgement on them. This would have occurred at the end of Dhii
al-Qa'da or early in Dhii d-Hijja of _**5**_ AH. But God knows best.
Similarly, Muhammad b. I s h q stated, "The conquest of Bann Qwayza
took place in Dhii al-Qacda and the beginning of Dhn al-Hijja. The polytheists
took charge of that pilgrimage."

_**ON THE EXECUTION OF ABU R4-FI' SALLAM B. ABU AL-HUQAYQ**_

Ibn Ishzq stated, "When the battle of al-khandaq and the Bann Quray~a affair

"Muhammad b. Musallam al-Zuhri related to me as follows, quoting 'Abd
AUzh b. Ka'b b. Malik as having said, 'God had so ordered it for His messenger
(SAAS) that Aws and Khazraj used to compete with one another like two
stallions. If Aws ever accomplished something for him, then Khazraj would
not want this to give them any advantageous position with h i over themselves.
So they would strive hard to achieve something similar. And when Khazraj
accomplished something, Aws would say the same.
"'When Aws struck down Ka'b b. al-Ashraf for his enmity to the Messenger
of God (SAAS), Khazraj determined that Aws would have no advantage with
h i over themselves thereby. And so they asked themselves who had expressed


IMAM ABU AL-FIDA' ISMA'IL IBN KATH~R **187**


an enmity similar to that of Ibn al-Ashraf; they thought of Ibn Aha al-Huqayq,
who was at Khaybar. They therefore asked permission of the Messenger of God
(SAAS) to kill him, and he agreed.
"'Five men of Khazraj, of Banii Salama, then set out to do this. They were
'Ahd All& b.'Atik, Mas'iid b. Sinan, 'Abd Allah b. Unays, Abii Qatada al-Harith
b. Rib'i, and Khuza'a b. Aswad, an ally of theirs from Banii Aslam. The Messenger

"'It was night when they arrived at the compound of Ibn Abii al-Huqayq.
They took care to close all the doors upon those who lived there. He himself

and asked to come in. His wife came out to them and asked who they were. They

The account proceeds, "'When we went in, we shut him and ourselves inside
the room, fearing someone might interfere between us. His wife screamed and

"'Then we left. 'Abd Allah b. 'Auk had poor sight and he fell off the ladder

"'We wondered how we could ascertain that he had died, so one of us

She then went close and, looking into his face, said, "He's dead, by the God of

"'When he returned and told us this, we carried our companion away and
reported to the Messenger of God (SAAS) the death of God's enemy. When

Ibn Ishaq stated, "Hassm b. Thabit spoke the following verses on this,

('Abd Allah's account went on), "'So I went in and hid. When everyone was

opened the gate. Aha Rafic was entertaining in an upstairs room of his. When his

"'When I reached his chambers, he was inside afigh, a dark apartment, but I

I left the chamber and went a little off, then came hack in again, asking, "What

thinking I had fmished (climbing down) I fell. It was a moon-lit night. I broke

Al-Bukhari, alone of the authors of the six canonical books of tradition,

I would comment that it is likely that when 'Abd All* h. 'Atik fell from
the ladder that he dislocated his shank and sprained his foot and his leg. When
he bound it up, it had the immediate effect of calming the pain. And when he
wanted to walk, he was aided (by unseen forces) for he was engaged in a beneficial
exercise. When he reached the Messenger of God (SAAS), and came to a rest,
the pain in his leg again flared up. When he stretched it out and the Messenger
of God (SAAS) touched it, that took away the pain there had been, as well as
what he might have expected there would be thereafter. This would reconcile
the former and latter accounts. But God knows best.

In this regard, M o s ~ b. Wqba related in his maghlizi, his work on the military

_**Chapter: The Mamage of the Prophet**_ _**`($US)`**_ _**to**_ **`Umm`** _**Habiba, daughter ofAbtl Suban**_


Al-Bayhaqi related following the battle of al-khandaq, quoting al-Kalbi from
Aha Sdih from Ihn 'Abhas, who said with relation to the words of the Almighty,
"Perhaps God will bring about friendship between you and those of them

marriage of the Prophet (SAAS) to Umm Habiba, daughter of Abii Sufyan;
she thus became the umm al-mu'mmin, the 'mother of the believers,'" while
Mu'awiya (son of Aba Sufym), became the khal al-mu'mmin, the 'uncle of the
believers'."

Al-Bayhaqi then stated, "Aha 'Ahd Allah al-Hztifiz recounted to us, quoting
A b a d h. Najda, quoting Yahya h. 'Ahd al-Hamid, quoting Ibn al-Muhwak,
from Ma'mar, from al-Zuhri, from Wrwa, who said that Umm Habiba was with
Wbayd All& h. J&sh who had gone to the Negus and had died. The Messenger
of God (SAAS) had then arranged marriage with Umm Habiba while she
was there in Abyssinia, and the Negus had arranged this, giving her a dowry
of 4,000 dirhams which he had taken to her by Shur&hil h. Hasana; it was he
who provided her trousseau, the Messenger of God (SAAS) not sending her
anything. He said, "The dowry provided for the wives of the Prophet (SAAS)
used to be 400 (dirhams)."
I would comment that in fact the dowries of the Prophet (SAAS) were 12
awqayya and 1 nash (of gold); and the wuqya was worth 40 dirhams, while the
nash was worth one-half (a wuqya). That totals 500 dirhams.
Al-Bayhaqi then recounted through Ibn Lahi'a, from Abii al-Aswad, from
Wrwa, that Wbayd Allah h. J&sh died a Christian in Abyssinia. The next to
marry Umm Habiba was the Messenger of God (SAAS); it was Wthman h.
'Affan, God he pleased with him, who arranged her marriage to him.

I comment that the conversion to Christianity of 'Ubayd Allsh b. Jahsh has
been described above. That occurred after he had migrated to Abyssinia with
the Muslims. There Satan subverted him and made Christianity seem attractive

What is authentic is the account of Yiinus, quoting Muhammad b. Ishaq, who

daughter of Abii Sufy~n. I have responded to the request made by the Messenger

of God (SAAS), who has given 400 dinars as her dowry." He then poured out

"'Khaid b. Sacid spoke, saying, "Praise be to God! I give H i praise and ask

I comment that it may well be that 'Am b. Umayya, when seen by <Amr b.
al-As emerging from the presence of the Negus, following the battle of al-khandaq,
had been active in the matter of Umm Habiba. But God knows best.

However, the _h & z_ al-Bayhaqi stated, "Aba 'Abd Allah b. Mandah related
that the marriage of the Messenger of God (SAAS) to Umm Habiba was in the
year 6 AH, while his marriage to Umm Salama was in the year 4 AH. **'**
I comment that Khalifa, Aba 'Ubayd Allah Macmar b. al-Muthanna and Ibn
al-Baraqi said the same, and that the marriage to Umm Habiba was in 6 AH.
Some people said that it was 7 AH. Al-Bayhaqi said, "That is more likely."
I also note that, as has been related heretofore, his marriage to Umm Salama
was late in the year 4 AH. It is likely that the marriage to Umm Habiba occurred
before that, though it could also have been thereafter. It is most probable that
it was following the battle of al-khandaq, because of what we have related
above regarding 'Amr b. al-'AS, and how he saw 'Amr b. Umayya with the
Negus, engaged in that matter. But God knows best.
The _**`hi@?`**_ Ibn al-Athir recounted in _al-Ghzba,_ quoting Qatada, that when
Umm Habiha migrated from Abyssinia to Medina, the Messenger of God
(SAAS) became engaged to her and married her.
Some scholars maintain that he married her after her father had accepted
Islam, following the conquest of Mecca. But that contradicts what was related
by Muslim, through 'Ikrima b. CAmmS al-Yamani, from Abii Zumayl Simxk b.
al-Walid, from Ibn CAbbas, that Abii Sufy2n said, "0 Messenger of God, grant
me three wishes!" "Yes," he replied. "That you give me authority to battle the
unbelievers just as I used to battle the Muslims." 'LYes," he replied. "And that
you appoint Mu'awiya as a clerk of yours." "Yes," he replied. "And I have at
home the best and most lovely of all the Arab women, Umm Habiba, daughter
of Abii Sufya; let me marry you to her."
That is the _hadith_ in its entirety.
Ibn al-Athir stated, "This _hadith_ is one for which Muslim is criticized. This is
because when Abii Sufyan came to renew the pact before the conquest, he went


**IMAM ABO AL-FIDA' ISMA'IL IBN** **KATHIR** **195**


in to see his daughter Umm Habiba and she rolled up the rug of the
Messenger of God (SAAS). He then asked, "By God, I don't know whether
you consider the carpet too good for me or me too good for it!" She replied,
"This rug belongs to the Messenger of God (SAAS), and you are a polytheist."
He replied, "I swear by God, you've changed for the worse since you left
me, daughter!"
Ibn Hazm stated, "This _**hadirh**_ was invented by 'Ikrima b. 'AmmiXr. This
statement from him should not be considered dependable."
Others stated that he wanted to renew the pact because of the disadvantages
in it (tbat had been included) without his permission. Others say it was because
he believed that his daughter's marriage would be dissolved because of his
acceptance of Islam.
But all this is unconvincing. What is most likely is that he wanted to marry
him (the Prophet (SAAS)) to his other daughter 'Amra, since he thought tbat
would bring honour to himself. And he therefore sought help from his daughter
Umm Habiba, as is stated in both _**~ahih**_ collections. The narrator was merely
in error in his using the name Umm Habiba. That is why we have given (only)

one report.
Abii 'Ubayd al-Qsim b. Sallh stated, "Umm Habiba died in the year 44 AH."
Abn Bakr b. Abii Khaythama said, "She died one year before Mu'zwiya." The
death of Mu'itwiya occurred in Rajab of 60 AH.


_**THE MARRIAGE OF THE MESSENGER**_ _**OF**_ _**GOD (SAAS) TO ZAYNAB,**_
_**DAUGHTER OFJAHSH B. RPAB B. YA'MUR B. SABRA**_ _**B.**_ _**MURRA**_ _**B.**_
_**KABiR B. GHANAM B. DUDAN**_ _**B.**_ _**ASAD B. KHUZAYMA, AL-ASADIYYA,**_

_**UMM AL-MVMINiN, 'MOTHER OF THE BELIEVERS'.**_


Her mother was Umayya, daughter of 'Ahd al-Murtalib, aunt of the Messenger
of God (SAAS). She was previously the wife of his freed-man Zayd b. ljnritha,
God be pleased with him.

Qatiida, al-Wiiqidi and some of the people of Medina said that he married her
in the year 5 AH; some added the month, Dhii al-Qa'da. The _**h ~ &**_ al-Bayhaqi
stated, "He married her after the attack on Banii Qurayza." Khalifa b. Khayyzy,
Abii Whayda Macmar b. al-Muthannit and Ibn Mandah said that he married her
in the year 3 AH. The first possibility is better known and it is the one accepted
by Ibn Jarir and several historians.
Various commentators, theologians and historians give as the reason for his
marrying her reference to a _**hadith**_ related by Ahmad b. Hanbal in his collection
that we have deliberately refrained from including so that those lacking understanding would not place it in the wrong context.+8


**48.** **Zaynah had originally been presented, when** **a** virgin, **by the Prophet** **(SAAS)** **to his freed-man**
**and adopted son Zayd d. Hnritha. Her later** **divorce** **and this marriage inspired much commentary**
**and is the subject of the following passage in** **the** **Qur'a** **quoted here by Ihn Kathir.**


**198** THE LIFE OF THE PROPHET **MUHAMMAD**


In His Glorious Qur'm, Ahnighty God stated, "And (consider) when you
say to him whom God had favoured and whom you had favoured, LKeep your
wife for yourself, and fear God,' and you hide within yourself what God makes
evident, and you fear men. Yet God has greater right that you fear Him. And
since Zayd has now finished with her, We give her to you in marriage so that
there should he no distress for believers regarding the wives of their adopted
sons when the latter have divorced them. God's command must be fulfilled.

And there should be no distress for the Prophet in accomplishing what God has
imposed upon him. Such has been God's course with those who went before.
God's decree is determined'" (s~rut _al-Ahz~k_ XXXIII, v.37, 38).
We have discussed this at sufficient length in our Tafsir (Exegesis).
The person referred to as having received God's favour is Zayd h. Hzritha, the
freed-man of the Messenger of God (SAAS). God favoured him with Islam, and
the Messenger of God (SAAS) also favoured him by setting him free and by
marrying him to Zaynab, daughter of Jahsh, the daughter of his own maternal
aunt. Muqatil b. Habba stated that the dowry he provided for her was ten
dinars and sixty dirhams, a veil for her head and face, a wrap, a coat of armour,
fifty **`mudd`** (a dry measure) and ten mudd of dates. She (Zaynab) remained with
him (Zayd) close to a year, or longer, but then they quarrelled. Her husband
complained about her to the Messenger of God (SAAS), and he would say to
him, "Keep your wife for yourself and fear God."
God stated, "You hide within yourself what God makes evident." Regarding
this, 'Ali b. al-Husayn Zayn b. alLCAbidin and al-Suddi said, "He (the Messenger
of God (SAAS)) knew that she was to be one of his wives and it is he who hid
(this) within himself."

Many early authorities discussed this matter in various strange ways. Some of
these are controversial and so we are omitting them.


God Almighty stated, "And since Zayd has now finished with her, We give
her to you in mamage ..." This refers to Zayd having divorced her. And when
her 'idda period was over, the Messenger of God (SAAS) sent to her so that
she would become engaged to himself, and he then married her. And it was the
Lord of the universe, Blessed and Almighty is He, who married him to her, as is
established in the ~ahih collection of al-Rukh%ri, from Anas b. Mzlik. The latter
related that Zaynab, daughter of Jahsh, used to claim superiority over the other
wives of the Messenger of God (SAAS) and say, "It was your families who
arranged your marriage, whereas it was Almighty God, from above the seven
heavens, who arranged mine!"
There is a report through Cisa b. Tahman, From Anas, which says, "Zaynab
would claim superiority over the wives of the Prophet (SAAS) and say, 'It
was God who arranged my marriage from heaven.' And it was regarding her
that the verse requiring use of the _hyab,_ the veil, was revealed, namely, _**`'0`**_ you

who believe, do not enter the chambers of the Prophet unless you are invited

Im%n Ahmad stated, "Hashim (meaning Ibn al-Q~im) related to us, quoting

_A n Account of the institution of the_ _hqzb,_ _the screen, on the_

It was appropriate for the screen to be instituted during this wedding, as a
protection for her and for her sisters, also known as the _**umahat**_ _**al-mu'mmin,**_ the
"mothers of the faithful". This was in accord with the previously held view of
Wmar Ibn al-Khat~b.


Al-Bukhari stated that Muhammad b. 'Abd Allah al-Raqqash related to him,

the Prophet.""'

Al-Bukhsi related this in other passages; and Muslim and al-Nasa'i did

I note that Zaynab, daughter of Jahsh, may God be pleased with her, was one of
the fust women who migrated. She was a woman of great goodness and charity.
At fust her name was Tarra, then the Messenger of God (SAAS) renamed her
Zaynab. She was known as Umm _**al-Hakam,**_ "al-Hakam's mother".

'A'isha, may God be pleased with her, said, "I never knew a woman more
religious, more God-fearing, more truthful in her speech, more protective of
family ties, more trustworthy or more charitable than Zaynab."
It **is** estahlished in both _**jahih**_ collections, as will he seen in the _**hadirh ~ l - i f k, ~**_
"the calumnious account", that 'A'isha stated, "The Messenger of God (SAAS)
asked Zaynab, daughter of Jahsh, about me. She was the (only) wife of the
Prophet who could compete with me for his favour. God encompassed her with
goodness, and she said, '0 Messenger of God, in all truth and obedience, I say I
never knew of her ('A'isha) anything but good.'"
Muslim b. al-Hajjsj stated in his _**~ahih**_ collection that M h t i d b. 'Ayliln
related to him, quoting al-Fadl b. Masa al-Shaybzni, quoting Talha b. Y&y% b.

Al-Bayhaqi stated, "People used to say that it was in Muharram of that year that
there was the expedition of Muhammad b. Maslama to Najd. It was during this
that they captured Thumama b. Athal al-Yamai."

I note, however, that in the text of Ihn Ishaq from Sa'id al-Maqburi, from
Aha Hurayra, that he (Abii Hurayra) was present then and it was after the
expedition against Khaybar that he (Aba Hurayra) emigrated. It (the expedition
to Najd) would therefore have to be dated thereafter. But God knows best.
It was during the early part of this year, for certain, that the expedition was
mounted against Banii Lihym.

Ibn Ishaq stated, "The conquest of Banii @rayza took place in Dhii dQacda
and the start of Dha al-Hijja. The polytheists had charge of the pilgrimage that
year, 5 AH that is." As is related above.
He went on, "The Messenger of God (SAAS) remained in Medina thereafter
for the months of Dha al-Hijja, Muharram, Safar and both Rabic al-Awwal
and Rabic al-Th&i. In Jumada al-Uwla, at the start of six months following the
conquest of Banii Qnrayva, he went forth against Bana Lihym seeking revenge
for Khubayb and his companions who were killed at al-Rajic. In order to surprise
the enemy, he made it appear that he was heading for Syria."
According to Ibn Hisha, he left Ibn **Umm** Makmm in command of Medina.
What Ibn Ish~q is referring to here is as follows. When the Messenger of God
(SAAS) had reached their homes (in his attack on Banii Lihyan) they retreated
before him and sought refuge in the mountain heights. He therefore turned
off to 'Usfiln, where he encountered a force of polytheists. It was there that he
performed the _**~aliit al-khawf;**_ the L'fear prayer".
This expedition has been described above as having occurred in 4 AH.
Al-Bayhaqi related it there.
But what Ihn Ishaq relates is most probable, namely that it took place after
the battle of al-khandaq. It is established that he did perform the _**fala al-khawf**_
at Wsfan on the expedition against Banii Lihyan. It should best, therefore, be

my camels. Go hack to your family, with God's blessings."'
Ibn Ishaq stated, "The _**hadith**_ on this subject was transmitted from Abn
al-Zuhayr al-Makki from al-Hasan al-Basri."


This, then, is this story with its text and lime of transmission as given by Ihn
Ishaq.

Al-Bukhm, God be pleased with him, states following his materials relating to
the al-Hudaybiyya incident and before his account of the expedition to Khaybar,
"The expedition to Dhn Qarad; this incident relates to the enemy's raid on the

to 'Abd al-Umsn h. 'Awf, who said, 'The milch-camels of the Prophet (SAAS)
have been stolen!' 'Who took them?' I asked. 'It was Banti Gha~afan,' he replied.
I called out three times, _'Wa_ _**sabaha.P**_ I (shouted so loudly I) made all between
Medina's two mountains hear me. I then rushed on ahead until I caught them

an archer. (As I did so) I called out, in _**rajaz,**_ doggerel verse, 'I'm Ihn al-Akwa',
and today the wicked will die!' I (continued shooting until) I had retrieved the

""'When the Prophet (SAAS) and his men arrived, I told him, 'Messenger
of God, I have prevented the enemy getting water. They will he thirsty. Send

he charitable!'


**IMAM ABU AL-FIDA' ISMA'IL IBN KATHIR** **`205`**


""'We then went back; the Messenger of God (SAAS) seated me on his camel

Muslim related it thus from Qutayha. Al-Bukhzri related it from Aha 'Aqim

Iman Ahmad stated that Hzshim b. al-@sim related to h i, quoting 'Ikrima

"I then climbed a hill, turned towards Medina and shouted three times, 'Yz
sabzhz!' I then pursued the enemy, bearing my sword and arrows. I began
shooting at them and wounding them; this was when there were plenty of trees
about. When one of the horsemen would come back at me, I'd sit at the base
of a tree and shoot. And every rider who came near I shot. As I shot at them,
I would call out, 'I'm Ibn al-Akwa'! Today the wicked will die!' When I would
attack one of their men on his mount, my arrows would fall on him until I
pierced him in the shoulder, then I'd cry out, 'Take that! I'm Ibn al-Akwa', and
today the wicked will die!'
"While I was in the trees, I plastered them with my arrows; when the mountain
trails were narrow, I would climb up the mountain side and hurl down rocks
on them. My engagement with them continued, with me following them and
calling out my battle cry, until God so arranged it that I retrieved and left behind
me all of the property of the Messenger of God (SAAS), having saved it from
their control. I went on shooting at them until I had got over 30 of their spears
and over 30 cloaks they were bearing. All of this they cast away I placed beneath
stones, gathering everything into position in the path the Messenger of God
(SAAS) would take. Later in the morning Wyayna b. Badr al-FazWi came to
reinforce them; at that point they were in a narrow defile. I climbed the mountain
so that I was above them. Wyayna asked them, 'What's this I see?' They replied,
'We've had too much trouble from this fellow. He's been with us from dawn till

now. He's seized everything we had and placed it all behind himself.' Wyayna
commented, 'Well, if this fellow saw that he was being hunted, he'd have left you

"Having made them hear my call, I asked them, 'Well, do you know me?'
'Who are you?' they asked. 'I'm Ihn al-Akwa',' I told them. 'By Him who

honoured Muhammad, none of you who pursue me will catch me, whereas

a l - R ~ m s n mounted al-Akhram's horse, but Aba Qatada closed with him and

"I went over to the Messenger of God (SAAS) and told h i, 'Please let

Muslim related this _&~d<th_ in this way with lines from 'Ikrima b. 'Ammxr in

Al-Bukh~i and al-Bayhaqi relate this engagement after al-Hudayhiyya and

Regarding the woman who escaped on the camel of the Prophet (SAAS), having

**212** THE LIFE OF THE PROPHET **M U H A M M A D**


_THE EXPEDITION AGAINST BAN0 AL-M USTALIQ OF KHUZA'A._


Al-Bukhai stated, "This was the expedition to al-Muraysi'."

Muhammad b. Ishaq stated, "That took place in 6 **AH."**
Mnsa b. Wqba, however, set it in 4 AH.
Al-Nu'mm b. Rashid stated, quoting al-Zuhri, "The _hadith al-@,i'_ the
'calumnious report', occurred during the expedition to al-Muraysic." Similarly
al-Bukhari related it from the military chronicle of Masa b. Wqba, to the effect
that it took place in 4 **AH.** However, it was related from both him and from Wrwa
that it occurred in Sha'bm, 5 AH. Al-Waqidi stated, "It took place when two nights
remained of Sha'bm in 5 **AH,** and he (the Prophet (SAAS)) was accompanied
by 700 men."
Muhammad h. Ishaq b. Yasar stated, following his account of the Dha Qarad
incident, "The Messenger of God (SAAS) remained in Medina for part of
Jumada al-Akhira and Rajah, whereafter he made an expedition against Banii

al-Mustaliq of Khuza'a, in Sha'bm, 6 **AH."**

Ihn Hishim stated, "He appointed Aha Dharr al-Ghifai in command of
Medina; Numayla b. 'Abd Allah al-Laythi, however, is also named."
Ibn Ishaq went on, "'Asim h. 'Umar b. Qatada, 'Ahd Allzh b. Aba Bakr and
Muhammad h. Yahya b. Hibbm related to me, each narrating part of the account
relating to the expedition against Bana al-Mus~aliq, as follows, 'The Messenger
of God (SAAS) was informed that Bana al-Mustaliq were assembling to attack
him, under the leadership of al-Haith h. Aha Dira, the father of Juwayriyya,
whom the Messenger of God (SAAS) later married. When he heard of their
activity, he went forth against them, engaging them at one of their water sources
at a place called al-Muraysi', near Qudayd, towards the coast. The forces met and
did battle; God defeated Bana al-Mustaliq, a number of them being killed, and
the Prophet (SAAS) took over as booty their women, children and possessions.'"

Al-Waqidi stated, "The Messenger of God (SAAS) went forth with two
nights having passed of Sha'ban in _**5**_ AH, with a force of 700 of his Companions
against Bana al-Mustaliq. They were allied to Bana Mudlij. When he reached
them, he entrusted the banner of the _muhqzrin_ to Aha Bakr, the Trusting - though
some say to 'Amma h. Yasir - and that of the _an@?_ to Sa'd h. Whada. He then
ordered Wmar b. al-Khatpb to tell the enemy, 'Cry out the words, _"La Ilaha tllz_
_Allah!",_ "There is no god but God". By this you will protect yourselves and your
property.' But they refused and cast arrows instead.
"The Messenger of God (SAAS) then ordered the Muslims to attack. They
did so as one. And not one man escaped them; they killed ten and captured the'
rest. Only one of the Muslims was killed."
It is related in both _~ahih_ collections, from a _hadiih_ of 'Abd Allah h. 'Awn,
who said, "I wrote to Nafi' asking him about the battle-cry prior to the fighting.
He replied, 'The Messenger of God (SAAS) attacked Bana al-Muspliq while

they were engrossed in their pleasures, taking water at the well. He killed their
warriors and took captives. It was that day he acquired - I think that is what
he said - Juwayriyya, daughter of al-HGth. 'Abd All& h. Wmar narrated this
to me, and he was with that army."'
Ibn Ishaq stated, "One of the Muslims, Hisham b. Suhaba, was struck down
that day. He was killed **in** error by one of the an@r who thought **`hi`** to be an

Ibn Ishaq related that Hisham b. Subaba's brother, Miqyas b. Subaba, arrived
from Mecca professing Islam and requested blood-money from the Messenger

"It assuaged me that he was felled in the valley, his
clothing stained with the blood of his jugular.
My mind was troubled before I killed him; my worries
kept me from enjoying my bed.
By killing him I eased my tension and got my revenge;
and I was prompt to return to the idols.
Through him I avenged Fihr and charged his blood-wit to
the chiefs of Banii al-Najjar, the lords of Fari' castle.""


I note that this is why this Miqyas was one of the four persons whom the
Messengef of God (SAAS) had executed on the day of the conquest of Mecca,
(having said) "... even if they be wrapped in the drapes of the ka'ba!"

Ibn Ishaq stated, "While the warriors were there at the well, a group of men

Ghifar named Jahjah b. Masad who led his horse. Jahjab and Sin% h. Wabr

"Zayd b. Arqam overheard this and so informed the Messenger of God
(SAAS), who had Wmar b. ai-Khatpb with h i at the time. Wmar advised him,

'Order 'Abbad h. Bishr to kill hi!' But the Messenger of God (SAAS) replied,

"'Ahd Allah h. Ubayy b. Saliil went to see the Messenger of God (SAAS)

"When the Messenger of God (SAAS) had set forth and travelled some

Miisa b. CUqba and al-Waqidi related this similarly.

Ihn Ishaq went on, "Then the _**siira**_ was revealed in which God made mention

I comment that I have written on this in my Tafsir (Exegesis) at sufficient

Ibn IshZq stated, "CAgim b. 'Umar b. Qamda related to me that 'Abd Allah b.
'Abd Allah b. Ubayy b. Saliil came to the Messenger of God (SAAS) and

"The Messenger of God (SAAS) replied, 'On the contrary, we will treat

_**THE**_ _**HUDAYBIYYA EXPEDITION**_


This indisputably took place in Dha al-Qa'da, 6 AH. Those who state this
include al-Zuhri, Nafic, freed-man of Ibn Wmar, Qatada, Mnsa b. Wqba and
Muhammad b. Ishzq b. Yasa, along with others too. This is also what was
related by Ibn **Lahi'a,** from Aba d-Aswad, from Wrwa - namely, that it
occurred in Dha al-Qacda of 6 AH.

Yacqab b. Sufyan stated, "Ismacil b. al-Khalil related to me, from 'Ali b.
Mushir (who said), 'Hisham b. Wrwa narrated to me, quoting his father as
having said, "The Messenger of God (SAAS) set out for al-Hudaybiyya in
Ramadan; (the agreement at) al-Hudaybiyya was made in Shawwd.""'

This is very strange to have come from Wrwa.
Both al-Bukhai and Muslim relate from Hudba, quoting Hammw, from
Qamda, that Anas b. Malik narrated to **`hi`** that the Messenger of God (SAAS)
performed the Lumra four times (sic) in Dhii al-Qcda, apart from the 'umra
performed along with his pilgrimage. The Hudaybiyya 'umra took place in Dha
al-Qa'da, that of the following year was in Dha al-Qa'da, that of al-JiCrana was
in Dbii alQa'da, when he divided up the booty from the Battle of Hunayn, and
there was the 'umra that took place along with his pilgrimage."
This is the wording of d-Bukhm.


Ibn Ish~q stated, "Thereafter the Messenger of God (SAAS) remained in
Medina for Ramadan and Shawwal; then, in Dhii al-Qacda, he left to perform
the 'umra, not to engage in warfare."
Ibn Hisham stated, "He appointed Numayla b. 'Abd All& al-Laythi in
command of Medina."

Ibn Ishsq went on, "He invited the local Arabs and the bedouin in neighbouring areas to accompany him, fearing that Quraysh would attack him or block
his way to the kacba. But many of the bedouin refrained from joining him.
"Eventually the Messenger of God (SAAS) set forth accompanied by men of
the muhzj~rin and the an@r and those bedouin who had joined him. He took with
him the animals for sacrifice and dressed in pilgrim garb so that people would
feel secure from attack by him and would recognize that he was only leaving to
visit this House that he wished to venerate.

Muhammad b. Muslim b. ShihXb al-Zuhri related to me, from Wrwa b.
al-Zubayr, from al-Miswar b. Makhrama and Marwan b. al-Hakam, as follows,
"The Messenger of God (SAAS) left in the year of al-Hudaybiyya intending to

for sacrifice and was accompanied by 700 men. Each sacrifice was for 10 persons.
Jabir b. 'Abd Allah used to say, so I have been told, 'Those of us present at

d-Hudaybiyya totalled **1,400."'**


Al-Zuhri stated, "The Messenger of God (SAAS) travelled as far as Wsfan,
where he met Bishr b. Sufyan al-Ka'bi, who told him, 'Messenger of God, these

out an arrow from his quiver and gave it to one of his Companions who took it

water and they had their mounts lie down there after they had been watered."

Ibn Ishzq went on, "A scholar related to me, from some men of Banii Aslam,

Al-Zuhri stated in his hadith, "When the Messenger of God (SAAS) had

Al-Zuhri stated, "Khuzn'a, both their Muslims and their polytheists, were

will see them.' When he saw them going past from the valley side, wearing their

without any sense!"'
Ibn Ishaq stated, "'Ahd All& b. Abti Bakr related to me that al-Hulays was

Al-Zuhri stated in his hadith, "Then they (decided to send) to the Messenger of

I saw the violence and bad language you directed at those who came back to you

"So he went to the Messenger of God (SAAS) and said, 'Muhammad, so have

"Aba Bakr, the Trusting, God be pleased with him, was behind the Messenger

Wrwa then asked, 'So who is this, Muhammad?' He replied, 'This is Ibn Abii

But now we are even.'

"Wrwa then began fondling the beard of the Messenger of God (SAAS),
while he was speaking to him. Al-Mughira b. Shu'ba, who was standing close by,

Aha Da'iid traced this tradition back with a line including Qurra, from Qatada.

Muslim also gave, from several lines of transmission, the following from Ihn

Muhammad b. Bash% included in the chain of authorities Aha Da1iid and

Shu'ba.


Al-Bukhm narrated it with 'Abd Allah as one of the authorities in the,
chain. Muslim narrated it from Wbayd Allah b. MuOdh, from his father, from

Al-Bukhzri is alone in giving this tradition. This text will follow complete

What is implied here is that all these accounts contradict what Ibn Ishaq
maintained, namely that those at al-Hudaybiyya were **700** in number.
He only said this  - though God knows best  - because he was using his
independent scholastic judgement; since there were **70** sacrificial camels, each
one of which would have been for ten men, then those making the sacrifice
would have been **700** in number.

But there is no need for all of them to have been participating in the offering,
nor that all of them were making the pilgrimage. It is established that the
Messenger of God (SAAS) sent out one group of them, who included Abii
Qatada. And Aha Qatada did not adopt the rhr~m state until after he had killed
that wild donkey which he and his companions ate. They carried some of it to
the Messenger of God (SAAS) while on the journey, and he asked (those in
a state of ahram), LLDid any of you order that he bring the meat or make any
gesture towards it?" "No," they said. "Then eat what remains of the donkey,"
he told them.

Al-Bukhari had stated, "Shu'ba h. al-Rabi' related to us, quoting 'Ali b.
al-Mubzrak, from Yahya, from 'Abd All& h. Aha Qatada, that his father (Abii

This text has additions and advantages that are absent from the narration of
Ibn Ishzq from al-Zuhn. His account quoted al-Zuhri from a group of others,
including Sufyan b. Wyayna, Macmar and Muhammad b. Ishaq. All of these
quoted al-Zuhri, from Wnva, from Marwiin and Miswar, in relating the narrative.

Marwm b. al-Hakam and al-Miswar b. Makhrama, from Companions of the
Messenger of God (SAAS), in relating the narrative.
This is the best chain of authority. For Marwxn and d-Miswar were young
at the time of al-Hudaybiyya. It is obvious that they acquired it from the
Companions, may God be pleased with them, in relating the narrative.

Al-Bukhzri stated, "Al-Hasan b. Ish~q related to us, quoting Muhammad b.

_**Chapter: On the Expedition and missions that**_ took _**place in**_ 6 _**AH.**_


The _**hhf;?**_ al-Bayhaqi, quoting d-Waqidi, gives a summary of these.


**61.** **The footnote of the Arabic printed ten reminds** **us** **that** **the** **statement comes** **in** **the context**
**of the conflict between** **'Mi** **and Muswiya over succession** **to** **the** **Caliphate.**


**242** THE LIFE OF THE PROPHET MUHAMMAD


In Rahic al-Awwal (or Rahic al-kkhir) of that year, the Messenger of God
(SAAS) sent Wkasha h. Mihsan with a force of **40** men to Ghanv Marziiq. They
fled from him and he encamped at their wells. He sent some men in pursuit of
them and took **200** of their camels which he led into Medina.

Also that year was the dispatch of Ahn Wbayda b. al-Jarr* to Dho al-Qivsa,
also with **40** men. He made for them on foot, reaching them in the morning while
it was still dark. They fled from him into the mountain heights. He captured
one of their men and brought him to the Messenger of God (SAAS).
And there was his dispatch of Muhammad b. Maslama with a force of **10**
men. The enemy hid from them until night; all the companions of Muhammad
h. Maslama were killed and he escaped, wounded.
That year too there was the mission of Zayd h. Haitha to al-Jamiim. A woman
of Muzayna called Ualima was captured and she directed them to one of the
places where Bana Salim were. There they captured cattle and sheep and took a
number of the polytheists prisoner. Among them was the husband of Halima;
the Messenger of God (SAAS) gave him to her and released them both.
Also that year was the mission of Zayd h. Haitha, in JnrnXdZ al-Uwla, to Banii
Tha'laba with a company of 15 men. The bedouin fled from him; he captured
**20** of their camels, then returned, having been absent for **4** nights.
Zayd b. Haitha also left in Jumada al-Uwla that year for al-'is.
He (al-Waqidi) also said, "That year the property that had been with Abii
alLCks h. al-Rahic was taken; he sought refuge with Zaynah, the daughter of the
Messenger of God (SAAS), and she took him in."

Ihn Ishaq related this man's story, about when the camels that were with him
were taken, his companions were killed and he fled from them and went to
Medina. His wife, Zaynah, the daughter of the Messenger of God (SAAS), had
emigrated after Badr. When he arrived in Medina, he sought refuge with her,
and she took him in following the _**al-subh**_ prayer. The Messenger of God (SAAS)
gave him over to her custody and told his men to return the camels taken from
him. They did return to him everything taken from him, so that he lost nothing.
When he returned with his property to Mecca and gave over to those he owed
what was due them from their deposits, he accepted Islam. He then left Mecca
and returned to Medina. The Messenger of God (SAAS) returned his wife to
him by the fmt marriage, not by remarriage or contract, as was related heretofore.
The period between his accepting Islam and her having emigrated was six years;
it is also said to have been two years.
We have explained that there is no discrepancy between the two accounts, and
that his acceptance of Islam came two years after the time when believing women
were prohibited to unbelievers. His acceptance of Islam came in 8 AH, in the
year of the conquest (of Mecca), not as is told above in the account of al-Waqidi
that it took place in 6 AH. But God knows best.

Al-Waqidi stated that in that year Dihya h. Khalifa al-Kalhi came hack from
Caesar, who had awarded him money and robes of honour. When he was at


**IMAM ABU AL-FIDA' ISML'IL IBN KATHfR** **243**


al-Husmz he was waylaid by some men of J u d h . They robbed him and left **`him`**
with nothing. The Messenger of God (SAAS) then sent out Zayd b. H%itha,
may God be pleased with him, against them.

AI-Wsqidi stated, "'Abd Allsb b. Ja'far related to me, from Ya'qab h. Wtba,
who said, "Ali, may God be pleased with him, went forth with 100 men to a
village of Bana Asad b. Bakr. This was because the Messenger of God (SAAS)
had learned that a group of their men wanted to extend help to the Jews
of Khaybar. He approached them at night, keeping hidden by day. He ('Ali)
captured a scout of theirs who confmed that he had been sent to Khaybar to
suggest to them that they hand over to them their dates."'

Al-Wzqidi, may God be pleased with him, said, "In Sha'bzn of 6 **AH** there was
the expedition of 'Abd al-Ralpm b. 'Awf to Damat al-Jandal. The Messenger
of God (SAAS) told him, 'If they obey, then marry _the._ daughter of their king.'
They did accept Islam and 'Abd al-Ra!unsn married their king's daughter,
Tamndur, daughter of al-Isba' al-Kalbiya; she was the mother of Aha Salama b.
'Ahd al-Rabnn b. 'Awf."


Al-Wnqidi stated, "In Shawwzl of 6 AH the expedition of Kurz b. Jsbir al-Fihri
against the people of Wrayni took place; they had killed the herdsman of the
Messenger of God (SAAS) and had stolen his cattle. The Messenger of God
(SAAS) sent Kurz b. J~bir with 20 horsemen to mck them down and they
retrieved them."

According to texts given by al-Bukhiiri and Muslim, quoting Sacid b. Aba
Wraba, from Qamda, from Anas h. Mdik, what happened was that a group from
Wkl and 'Urayna (from Wkl or Wrayna, according to one version) went to the
Messenger of God (SAAS). They told him, "Messenger of God, we're really
herdsmen, not farmers and we fmd Medina unhealthy." The Messenger of God
(SAAS) ordered them to leave with a small herd, in the charge of a shepherd,
and told them to live by drinking the milk and urine of the animals. They left
and when in the vicinity of al-Harra, they killed the herdsman of the Messenger
of God (SAAS), drove off the herd and denied Islam after having accepted it
earlier. The Prophet (SAAS) sent men in pursuit of them and had their hands
and feet cut off and their eyes gouged out; they were left there at al-Harra in that
state until they died.

Qatnda stated, "We have heard that thereafter, whenever the Messenger of
God (SAAS) made an address he would speak in favour of compassion and
against exemplary punishment."
This hadith is related by one group of scholars from Qatzda, while another
group relates it from Anas b. Mnlik.

In the account of Muslim, from Mu'zwiya b. Qum, from Anas, it is stated
that a group of Wrayna went to the Messenger of God (SAAS) and announced
their acceptance of Islam and their allegiance. Then smallpox broke out in
Medina, and they told him, "Since this smallpox has broken out, we'd like to go


244 **THE LIFE** **OF** **THE PROPHET** **MUHAMMAD**


back to the camels." He replied, "Yes; go and be with them." They did then
leave, but they killed the herdsmen and left with the camels.
According to that account, he sent some 20 of the an@r in pursuit of them,
along with an expert tracker. When they were found, their hands and feet were
severed and their eyes were gouged out.
In the sahib collection of al-Bukhzri, on a line of transmission through Ayyiib,
from Abn Qdzba, from Anas, who is quoted as saying, "A group from Wkal
arrived and accepted Islam. They loathed Medina and went to the Messenger of
God (SAAS) and told him so. He then said to them, "Then go and join the
camels; drink their milk and urine." They then left and lived among them for a
time; hut eventually they killed the herdsman and stole the camels. News of
this reached the Messenger of God (SAAS), and before the sun next arose they
had been brought to him. He had iron rods brought and these were heated and
used to cauterize them. He then had their hands and feet cut off and they were
dumped out in the heat, where they sought water. But they were given none
until they died, without protection.
In an account from Anas, he is quoted as saying, "I saw one of them biting the
ground in his thirst."
Abn Qdaba stated, "That gang murdered, stole and apostatized after having
declared their faith. They fought against God and His messenger (SAAS)."

Al-Bayhaqi related, through Wthmzn b. Aba Shayba, from 'Abd al-Rahmm
b. Sulaymm, from Muhammad b. Wbayd All&, from Abn al-Zubayr, from
Jzhir, that when the Messenger of God (SAAS) sent men in pursuit of them, he
said, _**`"0`**_ God, make them lose their way and make it narrower than a camel's
ankle." He went on, "They did lose their way and were captured and brought
back. He had their hands and feet severed and their eyes gouged out."
In the rahih collection of Muslim, it states, "The reason he had their eyes
gouged was that they had done this to the herdsman."


Section: Relating to happenings that year, 6 AH.


During that year the obligation of making the pilgrimage was revealed; dShzfifi'i
asserts that this came at al-Hudaybiyya in the words of the Almighty, "and
complete the pilgrimage and the 'umra for God" (serat al-Bagara; 11, v. 196).
This is why he (al-Shzfi'i) held the view that the pilgrimage could be deferred
and need not be performed as an urgent matter, because the Messenger of God
(SAAS) did not himself make the pilgrimage until 10 AH.
His view is opposed by the other three authorities, Maik, Aba Hanifa and
Ahmad (Ibn Hanbal). According to them, the pilgrimage is to be considered a
matter of urgency for all who can make it. They deny that its mujab, "necessity"
is deduced from the Almighty's words, "and complete the pilgrimage and the
'umra for God" but maintain that in this verse the requirement is only to finish
it once it has been commenced. They prove this through various citations, to


IMAM ABD AL-FIDA' ISMA'IL IBN KATH~R **245**


many of which we referred in our explanation of this verse in our Tafiir (Exegesis).
And to God is due all praise and credit.
It was during this year that Muslim women were forbidden to polytheists.
This was an exception to the general rule established by the truce agreed upon
at alaudaybiyya that year, namely that members of Quraysh were to be returned
to them even if wishing to accept Islam. And so the words of the Almighty
were revealed, _**'LO**_ you who believe! If believing women should come to you as
emigrants, then test them. God knows best about their faith. If you ascertain
them to be believers, then do not return them to the unbelievers. These women
are not permitted for marriage to those men, nor are those men permitted for
marriage to those women" (siirat al-Mumtahana; LX, v.10).

That year also there was the expedition to al-MuraysiC, during which the &at
al-zjZ, the calumnious report, arose which ultimately resulted in the Revelation
telling of the innocence of the umm al-mu'mmin, the mother of the believers,
'A'isha, as was related above.
The 'umra to al-Hudaybiyya occurred that year too, along with the blockade
made by the polytheists against the Messenger of God (SAAS). Ultimately
there resulted peace between them lasting ten years, during which time people
lived in security with one another on the understanding that there should be
neither fetters used nor swords drawn. Reference is made at length in the
appropriate places heretofore; and to God belong all praise and credit. That year
the polytheists had control of the pilgrimage.

Al-Waqidi stated, "In Dhn al-Hijja of that year, the Messenger of God (SAAS)
sent forth six men in the company of Hafib b. Abn Balta'a to al-Muqawqis, the
governor of Alexandria. He also dispatched Shujac b. Wahb b. Asad b. Judhayma,
who was present at Badr, to al-H&th b. Aba Shammar al-Ghassmi, the king of
the Christian Arabs, that is. Also he sent Dihya b. Khalifa al-Kalbi to Caesar, he
being Heraclius, emperor of Rome. And he dispatched 'Abd Allah b. Hudhafa
al-Sahmi to Chosroe, king of the Persians. Also he sent Salir b. 'Amr al-'Amiri
to Hawdha b. 'Ali al-Hanafi, and 'Amr b. Umayya al-Damri to the Negus, king
of the Christians of Abyssinia, his name being Ashama b. al-Hurr."


_**THE YEAR**_ _**7**_ _**AH. THE EXPEDITION AGAINST KHA YBAR,**_
_**EARLY THAT YEAR.**_


Shu'ba stated, from al-H&im, who quoted 'Abd al-Rahman b. Aba Lay12 as

Mnsa narrated, from al-Zuhri, that the conquest of Khaybar was in 6 AH;

Ibn Ish~q stated, "When the Messenger of God (SAAS) left Medina for

IMAM ABD AL-FIDA' ISMA'IL IBN KATHFR **247**


so they retraced their steps and stayed with their property and families, leaving

Al-Bukhai stated that it was related to him by CAbd All& b. Maslama, from

Al-Bukhwi stated that 'Abd Allah b. Maslama related to him, quoting H ~ t i m

'All~ihuhumma! _**`0`**_ God! Without You we would not have been
rightly guided,
Nor would we have given alms nor prayed.
We beseech You to forgive what we have done (wrong) -may
we be sacrificed for You!
We beseech you to send down Your serenity upon us
To make our feet secure when we meet our enemies.
And if they cry out trying to subvert us, we will
refuse.
Already have they loudly sought others' help against


US.'


"The Messenger of God (SAAS) asked, 'Who is this camel driver?' 'That's

"When the opposing forces were lined up for battle, 'Amir's sword was short,
and when he aimed it at a Jew's leg, the sharp blade swung back and injured his

Salama went on, "When they returned from battle, the Messenger of God
(SAAS) saw me (looking sad) and took me by the hand, asking, 'What is wrong?'

Muslim related this similarly from a _**hadith**_ of Hatim b. Ismncil and others,

_**'Wall0hi!**_ By God! Without God we would not have been

resist strongly.

we clash with the enemy.'

He went on to related the manner of his death much as al-Bukhm had done.

Ibn Ishaq stated, "A source I do not doubt related to me, from 'Am' b. Abu

This is a very anomalous _**hadith**_ indeed, from this line of transmission.


62. Since he had accidentally caused his own death rather than earned martyrdom at the hand

The _**hd.3**_ al-Bayhaqi related it from al-H&im, from al-Asamm, from alWyaridi, from Yiinus b. Bukayr, from Ibrahim b. Isma'il b. Mujmi: from Salih
b. Kaysm, from Abii Marw2n al-Aslami, from his father, from his grandfather,

Ihn Ishaq went on, "A source I do not doubt related to me, from Anas b. Mdik,

of God **(SMS).** On the way, we met the Khaybar labourers leaving

is most Great! Khaybar is mined! It's a bad day for an enemy we have warned

Al-Bukh~i stated that 'Abd All& b. Yiisuf related to him, quoting Malik,

Al-Bukhm is alone in giving this account; Muslim did not.
Al-Bukh%ri went on to state that Sadaqa b. al-Fad1 related to him, quoting

It's a had day for an enemy we have warned when we can dismount in their

The ha& al-Baybqi stated, "Ahii Tithiir, the jurist informed us, quoting Kha-b

**IMAM ABU AL-FIDA' ISMAqL IBN** **KATH~R** **251**


I comment that what is well established, in the _**sahih**_ collection of al-Bukhari
from Anas, is that the Messenger of God (SAAS) rode along with a Companion
at Khaybar and that in consequence his pants became pulled up to his thigh. It

It may be that this _**had&,**_ if true, makes it likely that he did ride donkeys on
some days, while he was besieging the enemy. But God knows best.
Al-Bukhari stated that Muhammad h. Sacid al-Khuzaci related to **`hi,`** quoting
Ziyad h. al-Rabic, from Abii ' I m m al-Jawni, who said, "Anas looked out at

Ihn Ishaq stated, "The Messenger of God (SAAS) then took possession of the
properties one by one as he conquered one fort after the next. The first of their
forts conquered was Nacm. There M&mad h. Maslama was killed; a millstone

Bann Abn al-Haqiq."
The Messenger of God (SAAS) acquired captives from them. These captives
included Safiyya, daughter of Huyayy b. Akhcab. She had been the wife of Kinma
b. al-Rabi' h. Abn al-Haqiq. Also captured were two of her female cousins. The
Messenger of God (SAAS) chose Safiyya for himself; Dihya b. Khalifa had
asked him for her; when the Messenger of God (SAAS) chose her for himself,
he gave to Dihya her two cousins.
The captives taken at Khaybar were distributed among the Muslims. The
men were eating the flesh of donkeys, and the Messenger of God (SAAS) issued
a proclamation against their doing this.

Al-Bukhsri devoted his attention to this and reported the prohibition from
excellent sources.

Its prohibition has been accepted by most scholars both early and later; all
four of the "orthodox Imams" prohibited its consumption.
However, some early authorities, including Ibn 'Abbzs, maintained that
eating it was permissible. These scholars offered varying reasons for discounting
the _**ahzdih**_ that have come down prohibiting it. For example, it was suggested
that the prohibition came because they were using the donkeys for transport.
Another reason given was that the prohibition related to the fact that the
donkeys were booty that had not yet been divided up into the (required)
fifths. It is also suggested that it related to the donkeys eating excrement, dung
that is.

The truth is that it was prohibited because of its nature. Authentic evidences
relate that the crier of the Messenger of God (SAAS) called out, "God and His
prophet prohibit your eating the meat of donkeys; it is unclean."
Affirmation of this is to be found in the work _**K~tab**_ _**al-Ahkam.**_

Ibn Ishaq stated, "Sallam b. Kirkira related to me, from 'Amr b. Dinar, from
Jabir b. 'Ahd Allah - Jabir himself not having been present at Khaybar - that


**IMAM** **ABU AL-FIDA'** **ISMA'IL** **IBN KATHiR**


when the Messenger of God (SAAS) prohibited people from consuming donkey
meat, he also allowed them to eat horsemeat."
The provenance of this is secure in both _**phih**_ collections, from a _**hadith**_ of
HammPd b. Zayd, from CAmr b. Dinar, from Muhammad b. 'Ali, from Jabir,
may God be pleased with him. He said, "At Khaybar, the Messenger of God
(SAAS) prohibited eating the meat of donkeys and gave permission for horses
(to be eaten)."
This is the phraseology given by al-Bukhari.
Ibn Ishaq stated, "'Abd Allah b. Abii Najih related to us, from Makhiil, that
the Prophet (SAAS) prohibited four things that day: intercourse with pregnant
women, eating domestic donkeys, eating carnivorous animals, and selling the
spoils of war before their (official) allotment."
This _**hadith**_ is _**mursal,**_ lacking proper transmission back to the Prophet (SAAS).


Ibn Ishnq stated, "Yazid b. Aba Habib related to me, from Abii Marziiq, Najib's

a man who believes in God and the last day to have intercourse with a captive

a man who believes in God and the last day to sell any spoils of war before its
allotment. It is not permissible for a man who believes in God and the last day to
ride any mount from the captured stock of the Muslims and then to return it
when it is exhausted. Nor is it permissible for a man who believes in God and the
last day to wear any clothing from the captured stock of the Muslims and then
to return it when it is worn out.'""

Abii Da'ad narrated this similarly through Muhammad b. Ishaq. Al-Tirmidhi

Ayyab, from Rabi'a b. Salim, from Bishr b. 'Ubayd Allah, from Ruwayfic b.
Thabit in abbreviated form. He characterized the _**hadith**_ as _**hasan,**_ "good".
In the _**phih**_ of al-Bukhm, from N%fiC, from Ibn Wmar, it is stated that
the Messenger of God (SAAS) at Khaybar prohibited the meat of domestic
donkeys, and also the eating of garlic.
Ibn Hazm narrated, from CAli and Shurayk b. al-Hunbal, that they accepted
the prohibition of onions and raw garlic. What al-Tirmidhi transmitted from them
was that (use of them) constituted _**a17karaha,M**_ a practice considered repugnant.
But God knows best.

People speak of the _**hadith**_ given in both _**jahih**_ collections through al-Zuhri,
from CAbd All& and al-Hasan, sons of Muhammad b. al-Hanafiyya, from their
father, from his father 'Ali b. Aba Tdib, may God be pleased with him, that the
Messenger of God (SAAS) prohibited at Khaybar _**nrkzh al-mutca,**_ 'Ltemporary
marriage", and (eating) the meat of domestic donkeys.
This wording in both _**jahih**_ collections comes down through MSik and others,
from al-Zuhri. This _**hadith**_ requires that the prohibition of _**nrk~h al-mut'a**_ applied
only to the battle at Khaybar.
This is problematic, from two viewpoints. One is that at the battle of Khaybar
there were no/women to be so married, and their having captive women obviated
temporary marriage.
The second problem is that it is established in the _**sahib**_ of Muslim, related
from al-Rabic b. Sabra, from Ma'bad, from his father, that the Messenger of
God (SAAS) gave permission to engage in _**al-mut'a**_ at the time of the conquest
(of Mecca), but then prohibited it before he had left Mecca, saying, "God has
prohibited it until Judgement Day."
According to this, then he would have prohibited it, then permitted it and
then for it to have been again prohibited. This would have required there to have
been abrogation twice. And that is unlikely.

Al-Shnfici, moreover, stated that he knew of nothing that had ever been
permitted thcn prohibited, then permitted and again prohibited, apart from
_**nrk~h al-mut'a.**_ And the only reason he made the exception for this was because
he was relying upon both these traditions referred to above.
Al-Suhayli and others quote scholars who claim that it was permitted three
times and prohibited three times. Others state that this happened four times.
This is most unlikely. But God knows best.
The authorities differ as to when was the frst time it was prohibited. Some
say at Khaybar, others at the _**cumrat al-qad~',**_ others in the year of the conquest
(of Mecca); this latter seems the most likely. Others say it was first prohibited at
Am% (a time close to that of the alternative preceding it); others say at Tabak,
others at the _**hijut al-ma&',**_ the "farewell pilgrimage".
Abii DPad related this.

Some scholars refute the _**hadith**_ related from 'Ali, may God be pleased with
h i, by saying that it contains _**taqdim ma ta'khir,**_ "an inaccurate sequencing of
time".

The best alternative seems to be what the Im- A h a d related, as follows,
"Sufym related to us, from al-Zuhri, from al-Hasan and 'Abd All&, the two sons
of Muhammad (b. al-Hanafiyya) from their father. Hasan was the more convinced
of the two that 'Ali had said to Ibn 'Abbns, 'The Messenger of God (SAAS)
prohibited _**nrkah al-mut'a**_ and eating the meat of domestic donkeys at Khaybar.'"
They said, "The narrator believed that the mention of Khaybar was the time
and place for the prohibition of both, that was not so, however, since it was one
only for the prohibition of donkey meat. There is no time and place mentioned


IMAM ABU AL-FIDA' ISMACIL IBN **KATHiR** **263**


in fact for nrkzh almut'a. He included this only because 'Ali, may God be
pleased with him, learned that Ibn 'Ahb3s had permitted the nikah al-mut'a and
the meat of donkeys, as is well known. And the Commander of the Believers,
('Ali) therefore told him, 'You are misguided. The Messenger of God (SAAS)
prohibited nrkzh al-mut'a and the meat of domestic donkeys at Khaybar.'"
He joined both together in this prohibition for him so that he would retract
what he had considered permissible.
Our teacher, the Abii al-Hajjsj al-Mizzi, may God encompass **`hi`** in his
mercy, tended to accept this explanation.
Nevertheless, Ibn 'Abbns did not retract the permission he had given regarding
donkey meat and temporary marriage. He attributed the prohibition against
eating donkeys to the fact that they were their baggage animals. As for temporary
marriage, he only rendered this permissible in case of need while travelling. As
for the prohibition, that referred to when the circumstances involved indulgence
of wealth or lust. Various of his associates and followers have adopted his position.
This was well known to be the view of the scholars of Hiju up to the time of Ibn
Jurayj and beyond.
There is an account relating that Imam Ahmad b. Hanbal took the same
position as Ibn 'Abbzs; however, this account is weak.
Certain persons who adhere to the view of permissibility try to relate an
account from the I m m ( m a d ) to the same effect. This also is inauthentic, but
God knows best. The text relating to this is in the KztZb al-AhkZm. And help is
sought through God.

and discovered the mark made on her cheek by her husband's blow. He asked her
about this, and she related to him what she had seen in those wonderful visions.
May God he pleased with her and grant her pleasure.

AlLcAhb% requested, as did 'Ali on behalf of Fatima, since they had failed

Fatima, may God be pleased with her, was annoyed with him about this
and experienced some anger. Yet this was not appropriate for her. She and all
the Muslims well knew his position and standing with the Messenger of God
(SAAS) and his role in assisting him both during his life and after his death. May

Fauma, may God be pleased with her, died six months thereafter. 'Ali then
renewed his oath of allegiance. During the Caliphate of Wmar b. al-Kha~sb,
they asked him to give control of this _**Sadaqu**_ to 'Ali and al-'Abb~s. They
pressured him through a group of the Companions. And Wmar, may God be
pleased with him, agreed to this. He did so because of the multiplicity of his
duties, the extensiveness of his domain and the great spread of his subjects.

'Ali gained advantage over his uncle alLCAbb% in this matter. Then they
accompanied each other and quarrelled in front of Wmar. And they brought
along a group of the Companions to him and asked him to divide up the
assets between them in such a way that each would be independent of the other.
But Wmar resisted this strongly, fearing that such a division would he similar
to the division through inheritance. He said, "Look after it together. And if
you can't, then turn it over to me. By Him at whose command the heavens
and earth stand, I'll never reach any other decision about this!" The property
continued to be managed in this way, by their descendants, into the 'Abhaside
era, the expenditures continuing to he made as they had been by the Messenger
of God (SAAS). (This is what became of) the assets of Bana &Nadir, from
Fadak and the share of the Messenger of God (SAAS), from Khayhar.

Al-Bayhaqi related that Banii Fazaa wanted to do battle against the Messenger
of God (SAAS) on his way back from Khaybar and assembled for this purpose.
He then sent a messenger to them suggesting a specific site for the battle. Having
ascertained this, they fled as fast as they could, moving far outside his path.
The Messenger of God (SAAS) proceeded further and when Safiyya was free of
her period he consummated his marriage with her at a place called Sudd al-Sahbal,
on his route to Medina. He served _**hays**_ for a wedding feast and stayed there with
her for three nights. She accepted Islam and he freed her and married her. He gave
her freedom as her dowry. She was one of the _**ummahat al-mdminin,**_ 'mothers of
the believers' as his Companions understood when he placed a veil over her
when she rode behind him on the same mount. May God be pleased with her.
Muhammad b. Ishaq related in his biography of the Prophet (SAAS) as

of God (SAAS) saw him there, he asked him, 'What is wrong, Abii Ayytib?' He
replied, 'I was afraid for you from this woman. She is a woman whose father,
husband and people you have killed. And until recently she was a disbeliever. So

Ibn Ishaq stated, "When Khayhar had been conquered, the Messenger of God
(SAAS) talked with al-Hajjnj b. 'Ilat al-Sulami, of the sub-tribe of Bahz, who
asked him, 'Messenger of God, in Mecca I own money in the possession of my
wife Umm Shayba, daughter of Aha T&a (she had earlier borne him his son
Mu'rid h. al-Hajjaj) and I also have other funds held by various merchants there.
Please allow me to go there.' He did so. Al-Hajjaj then said, 'Messenger of God,
I'll he forced to speak lies.' 'Do so,' he told him.


**292** **THE LIFE OF THE PROPHET MUHAMMAD**


"Al-Hajjiij stated, 'I travelled to Mecca and at the pass al-Baydii' there were
men of Quraysh listening for news and asking about the activities of the
Messenger of God (SAAS). They had heard that he had gone to Khaybar, which
they knew to be the chief village of Hija, productive, well-fortified and well
populated. They were seeking information from travellers.
"'When they saw me, they said, "It's al-Hajjaj h. 'Ilii!." (They did not know
of my acceptance of Islam.) "He'll have news, by God. Tell us, Abn Muhammad.
We have learned that al-Qa.t6, %he breaker of family ties', has gone off to
Khaybar, a town of Jews and the 'farm of the Hija'." I replied, "I heard that too;
and I have news that will please you." They crowded at both sides of my camel
asking, "Well, what is it, Hajjaj!" I replied, "He has been badly defeated, such _**ils**_
you could never imagine. Very many of his men have been killed and Muhammad
has been taken captive. And they (the Jews) have said, 'We'll not kill him;
instead, we'll send him in to Mecca where they can kill him among themselves
in revenge for those of their men he killed."' (Hearing this) the Quraysh men
went off into Mecca shouting, "News has arrived! You need only wait and
Muhammad will he brought in to be killed among you!"'

"Al-Hajj@ went on, 'I asked them, "Please help me collect the money I own
and is owed me in Mecca; I want to go to Khaybar and acquire the spoils from
Muhammad and his men before some other merchants precede me there." And
they did, gathering my assets faster than I had ever heard before. I then went
to my wife and said, "I want my money," (I had left money there with her), "for
I want to go to Khayhar to seize opportunities to buy before other merchants
precede me there."
"'When alLcAbbiis b. 'Abd al-Muttalibn heard the news and about myself, he
came and stood beside me in the tent of a merchant. He asked, "Hajjiij, what
news is this you bring?" I replied, "Could you keep safe what I might entrust
with you?" "Yes," he answered. "Then wait", I told him, ''till I can meet you
alone; I'm collecting my funds, as you can see; please leave me until I fmish."
When I had fmished getting together everything I had in Mecca and was ready
to leave, I met al-cAbha~ and said, "Aha al-Fadl, keep private what I tell you for
three days, because I fear pursuit. After that, say whatever you like." "I agree,"
he said. I then told him, "I left your nephew the bridegroom of their king's
daughter" -meaning Safiyya, daughter of Huyayy - L'after he had conquered
Khaybar and had taken away all it contained for himself and his men." "What
are you saying, Hajjaj?" be asked. "It's true, by God," I assured him, "hut keep
it confidential about me. I have accepted Islam and only came for my money
fearing it might he seized. When three days have elapsed, you can tell what you
know as ever you want."
"'On the third day, al-'Ahbas dressed in a fine robe, put on perfume, took his
walking stick and went out to the ka'ba, which he perambulated. When people

"God now reverted to the polytheists that depression that had been upon the

The chain of authorities for this _hadith_ meets the criteria of both the great
authorities. Yet only al-NasZ'i of all six authors of the great collections of _**ahadith**_
included it. He quoted IshZq h. IbrZhim, from 'Abd at-RazzZq, and his _hadith_
is similar.

The _hcif;?_ al-Bayhaqi related it through M&miid b. Ghaylan, from 'Abd
al-kzaq. He also related it through Ya'qiih b. Sufym, from Zayd b. al-Mubd,

Miis b. Wqba similarly stated in his work on the military engagements

as above. But God knows best.

Al-Suhayli, may God be pleased with him, stated, "On the reason for al-Hajj~j
